headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network capabilities create default data-leakage, prompt-injection, and cascading-error risks between AutoGen and OpenHands.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write configured working directories and OpenHands can read/write files in its runtime sandbox, so a shared filesystem or mounted volume could let attacker-controlled content flow from one agent into the other as instructions. This is not proven by default, but the pair has a plausible bridge and both agents parse file content during agent loops.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or mounted volume
IF one agent treats file contents as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents
Add a provenance header check before parsing files
Use read-only mounts for cross-agent handoff files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing middleware between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and have broad network egress, so any shared workspace can expose application data from AutoGen to OpenHands and onward to model providers or APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so this is not high, but the leakage pathway is realistic in common orchestration setups.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace or volume
IF either agent forwards file contents to a remote model provider or API
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Restrict network egress for one agent during handoff
Redact secrets before writing shared files
Audit mounted volumes for sensitive data
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and execute shell commands, while OpenHands can also write the filesystem, modify git state, and run browsers. If they share a writable repo or directory, concurrent edits and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. The overlap is broader on OpenHands, so the pair is dangerous in default multi-agent orchestration unless isolated.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable repository or directory
IF git operations occur without external locking or serialization
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Serialize write phases with a lock file
Disable git writes for one agent
Review and merge changes manually after each turn
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool calls and code execution results, and OpenHands runs an agent loop with shell/browser/editor actions. If OpenHands consumes AutoGen output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious instruction can cascade into real actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses AutoGen-produced text as direct task instructions
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks the handoff
mitigations: Require explicit confirmation before actions
Insert a validation step between agents
Limit OpenHands to dry-run mode for handoffs
Log and diff every proposed action
requires-engineering: add schema-validated task contracts

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only state generic application data or mounted files, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. Because the compliance surface is underspecified, I cannot prove a breach pathway; the other agent is not cited separately because no distinct compliance obligation is shown for either profile.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either runtime without a matching policy
IF one deployment has stricter retention or residency rules than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both runtimes
Document retention and residency settings
Use separate tenants for sensitive workloads
Review logging defaults before deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for regulated data
